question.text: What is the maximum QIP issue size relative to the issuer's net worth under SEBI ICDR?

answer.text: No limit relative to net worth

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the SEBI (ICDR) Regulations, the aggregate amount raised by an issuer through a QIP in any financial year is capped at 5 times the net worth of the issuer as per the audited balance sheet of the previous financial year. This dilution ceiling is a structural safeguard intended to prevent disproportionate equity expansion through the QIP route. The Trap: "3 times the net worth" and "10 times the net worth" are plausible-sounding but incorrect multiples. "No limit relative to net worth" is tempting because QIPs are placed with sophisticated QIBs who can assess dilution themselves, but SEBI still imposes the 5x ceiling as a regulatory safeguard. Note: The 5x net-worth QIP issue-size cap is not present in the QIP section of the cited NISM Series IX Merchant Banking workbook pages (which cover eligibility, the two-week gap between consecutive QIPs, monitoring agency thresholds, pricing, minimum allottees, and lock-in). The "5 times net worth" rule above is referenced from the SEBI (ICDR) Regulations as general regulatory knowledge, not from the cited workbook chapter.
